context.situation: I run launch operations for a heavy-lift vehicle. Tomorrow is our first commercial payload and the window is narrow. Overnight temperatures will be well below anything we have launched in. Component engineers at our supplier have raised a concern about seal behaviour in cold conditions and recommended we wait. Their data is a scatter of prior flights and they cannot give me a temperature threshold. We have flown successfully in colder-than-spec conditions twice. Two further delays would put the programme's commercial credibility at risk, and I have asked the supplier to come back with evidence that it is unsafe to fly.
context.whatMatters: Maintaining the launch schedule and commercial credibility.
context.stakeholders: Launch team, supplier management, supplier engineers, payload customer, crew families.
context.uncertainties: Seal behaviour at the forecast temperature; meaning of sparse flight data.

evidence.text: Supplier engineers recommended delaying until temperatures rise.
The supplier could not identify a specific temperature threshold when asked.
We have flown below specification temperature twice without failure.
I asked the supplier to demonstrate that it is unsafe to fly.
The supplier's management subsequently reversed their engineers' recommendation.
I take the reversal as evidence the concern was not substantial.
Two prior delays have already been reported publicly.
